system_overview: A small invite-only web service for a private group of friends to store recipes, plan weekly menus on a shared calendar, and generate a unit-aware merged grocery list. A single server-rendered web app with a relational store and one nightly reminder job keeps operations near zero.

recommended_language.rationale: Dozens of users and near-zero ops budget make raw performance irrelevant; the hard part is unit-aware ingredient merging, where Python's mature parsing and quantity libraries (e.g. pint) remove the riskiest custom code. Chosen on technical fit to the merge problem, not familiarity.

quality_goals.goal: Grocery merge is always correct or visibly conservative (never silently wrong)
quality_goals.driver: quality_goals: correctness of unit-aware merge above all

quality_goals.goal: Runs unattended for months on one cheap box

architecture_decisions.title: Single server-rendered web app
architecture_decisions.rationale: A few dozen users and a solo maintainer make any service split pure overhead; one process serves pages, API, and the reminder scheduler.

positive: One deployable unit to host cheaply
No client build pipeline to maintain
negative: A future native mobile client would need an API extraction

ruled_out.rejection_reason: Doubles the deployable surface and adds a JS build chain for a browser-only hobby tool with no stated interactivity needs.

architecture_decisions.title: Literal-first ingredient merge with curated conversions
architecture_decisions.chosen_option: Merge identical units literally; convert only via a checked-in conversion table; list incompatibles side by side
architecture_decisions.rationale: Silent unit guessing is the main correctness risk; a conservative merge with explicit conversions keeps wrong quantities out of the list.

positive: Merge errors become visible duplicates instead of wrong amounts
Conversion table grows with real usage
negative: Early lists show occasional duplicate lines until the table fills in

ruled_out.rejection_reason: Non-deterministic output is unacceptable for the one feature whose correctness the user named as critical.

oss_components.name: pint
oss_components.purpose: Unit parsing and conversion for ingredient quantities
oss_components.why_selected: Mature, widely used quantity library; replaces the riskiest custom code in the system

what_not_to_build: A custom unit-conversion engine (use pint plus a small curated food table)
User-facing public signup, password reset flows, or OAuth — invite links cover the stated security posture
A mobile app or offline sync layer nobody asked for

risk_flags.risk: Email deliverability from a hobby server lands reminders in spam
risk_flags.mitigation: Send through a free-tier transactional email provider instead of raw SMTP from the app box.

open_questions: Should manual grocery-list edits survive menu changes (merge regeneration policy)?
constraints: Single cheap deployment target; one process must serve everything
Grocery merge must never silently produce wrong quantities
